Tom Morgan Sports News Correspondent, in Miami Published 22 June 2026 7:00am BST Given his penchant for seeking the limelight, the absence of Donald Trump is perhaps the great shock of this World Cup so far.While his politics have pervaded the tournament – from travel bans on countries to forcing Iran to train in Mexico – the president is missing. Despite all that action on the pitch and the glare of the world’s biggest television audiences, Trump has gone AWOL.Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House’s World Cup taskforce, insists his boss is revelling in the guessing game of when he might appear. “He likes a good cliffhanger, right?” Giuliani told The Telegraph.A fortnight into the tournament, Trump has failed to show at any of the games in his own backyard, including the US’s two thumping victories. Gianni Infantino, Fifa’s all-powerful president, is in regular contact with Trump but has been unable to secure what he craves perhaps more than anything: a photo opportunity with his friend at one of the games. Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, will be desperate for a photo opportunity with his friend Trump Credit: Jim Watson/AP The Telegraph has been told Trump is now unlikely to show up before the final in New Jersey on July 19, where he is expected to present the trophy.It is also possible he will put in an appearance before that, but only if the US reach the semi-final, which would be held in Dallas on July 14, according to sources familiar with the situation. That would, incidentally, be the 101st match of the tournament.“The president is preoccupied with the US’s July 4 celebrations. The World Cup just isn’t on his radar at the moment,” a well-placed source said. “He will give the trophy at the final, but I don’t think we will see him before then. It’s possible he’ll go to a semi-final, but only if the US get that far.”But a president known for his capriciousness could just decide at the last minute he fancies a game of football. At any time and at any place. That presents its own security nightmares, for the presidential detail and fans alike.Trump skipped the opening match in Mexico, which he despises and which despises him, but also the opener in the US, where the co-hosts beat Paraguay in Los Angeles. The United States have taken the World Cup by storm so far, but there is still no sign of the president Credit: Patrick T Fallon/AFP via Getty Images This was supposed to be, for good or bad, Trump’s World Cup. Sports mad and ever eager for the global limelight, the World Cup seemed the perfect fit.Fans had certainly expected him, with derogatory chants honed but so far unheard by the president. Those will probably have to wait for the final – unless Fifa officials can work out how to stop them. Trump’s appearances at sporting events are a security nightmare, causing hours of delays to fans trying to get into arenas.Australian supporters, at their opening game against Turkey, chanted en masse: “Aussie boys are on a bender, Donald Trump is a sex offender,” a slur that is false but likely a reference to his one-time friendship with the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, or else to the findings of a civil court case in New York in 2023 that he had sexually abused a female magazine columnist who was awarded $5m damages. Trump is seeking to overturn the verdict at the Supreme Court. England supporters have sung: “He’s fat with piles, he’s in the Epstein files...” England fans have had some fun at Trump’s expense Credit: Jeffrey McWhorter/Shutterstock Trump has pointed out he had broken off all contact with Epstein after the two men fell out around 2004, prior to Epstein’s child sex conviction.There is no suggestion Trump is avoiding the tournament to avoid the verbal abuse.
